rationale: M49 W21 (#850). Pins Java-reserved words as named-argument KEYS. `open`, `module`, `record`, `with` and `sealed` are Java keywords and this grammar extends Java, so `map_item` — whose key accepts `identifier | literal | (expr)` — could not accept them, while every other name position in the grammar already accepts `_reserved_identifier` (five sites: `field('name', choice($.identifier, $._reserved_identifier, …))`). The failure was not local: `exclude group: 'a', module: 'b'` failed to form a map_item and dragged its enclosing command block into ERROR recovery, which is why the `.gradle` census's largest first-error signature was a bare `ID {`. MEASURED pre/post on this exact file through the production analyzer: pre-fix 0 symbols and 1 relationship (a single collapsed `uses conf -> exclude` at 13 — the class body never became a class), post-fix 5 symbols and 7 relationships. Corpus impact, grails-core @ a83f8748, 454 *.gradle files through parseFile: parse-failing 86 (18.9%) -> 21 (4.6%), relationships 15,013 -> 17,017, with the failing-file SETS compared file-by-file — 65 fixed, 0 regressed, 0 files losing relationships. `authoredBeforeAnalyzerRun` is false because the expectation was read off the corrected emission; the two counts above are the provenance. The parse-clean property is pinned by F9; this file pins the analyzer-visible consequence (the enclosing class and its methods exist at all, and the command is a CALL not a READ).
